description: An address form whose fields and validation adapt per country instead of assuming US format.

files.content:
# International Address Form

Most address forms are built for one country and bolted onto everywhere else — a rigid 5-digit ZIP field that rejects a UK postcode, a hard-coded US state dropdown for a Nigerian customer. Anyone shipping outside that one country hits friction that has nothing to do with whether their address is actually valid.

## The solution

An address form whose fields and validation rules change based on the country you pick. US gets a state dropdown and a ZIP pattern; UK gets a postcode pattern; Nigeria gets a state dropdown and an optional postal code; anything else falls back to a generic set of fields. Validation is inline, per-field, with accessible error messages tied to their inputs via `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`.

## How to use it

1. Open `index.html` in a browser.
2. Pick a country — the fields below update to match.
3. Fill in the address and submit. Invalid or missing required fields get a specific inline error; valid submissions show a success message.

## How it's built

Plain JavaScript, no dependencies. Each country is a config entry listing its fields (id, label, whether it's required, an optional `<select>` options list, and an optional validation `pattern` + `hint`). Changing the country re-renders the field set from that config; validation runs the same config against `FormData` on submit, so adding a new country is just adding a new entry — no new logic.

## Contribute

- Add Canada (province dropdown, postal code pattern `A1A 1A1`).
- Add live validation on blur, not just on submit, so errors show up before someone tries to submit the whole form.
- The "Other" fallback country has no postal code pattern at all — consider a loose length-based sanity check instead of no validation.

Scaffolded by an automated weekly pipeline, then refined by hand — see the factory repo for how it works.

Shipping address

Fields and validation adapt to the country you pick — no more forcing a Nigerian address through a 5-digit US ZIP field.

issue.title: Add Canada as a supported country
issue.body: Add a `CA` entry to the `COUNTRIES` object in `app.js`: street, city, a province dropdown (use the 13 provinces/territories), and a postal code field validated against the Canadian format `A1A 1A1` (letter-digit-letter, space, digit-letter-digit, case-insensitive). Follow the same shape as the existing `US` or `NG` entries — no other code changes needed, the form renders and validates from this config automatically. Good first issue, under an hour.
